name: Jumping Jacks
summary: Classic full-body heart-rate raiser.
steps: Stand tall, feet together, arms at your sides.
Jump feet wide while swinging arms overhead.
Jump back to the start and keep a steady rhythm.
cues: Stay light on the balls of your feet
why: Gets blood moving and warms the ankles before any skating-style movement.

name: High Knees
summary: Fast running in place, knees to hip height.
steps: Run in place, driving one knee up to hip height.
Pump your arms like you're sprinting.
Keep a fast, quiet foot contact.
why: Primes hip flexors for stride recovery: the knee drive that brings your leg back under you.

name: Front-to-Back Leg Swings
summary: Dynamic hip swing through flexion and extension.
steps: Hold a wall or post for balance.
Swing one leg forward and back like a pendulum.
Gradually increase the range. Switch legs.
why: Opens up the hip range you need for a long, powerful stride.

name: Lateral Leg Swings
summary: Side-to-side swing across the body.
steps: Face a wall with both hands on it.
Swing one leg across your body, then out to the side.
Go a bit wider each rep. Switch legs.
cues: Keep hips square to the wall
why: Groin strains are one of hockey's most common injuries. This wakes up the adductors before load.

name: Walking Lunge + Twist
summary: Lunge forward and rotate over the front leg.
steps: Step into a long lunge.
Rotate your chest toward the front knee, arms extended.
Return to center, step through into the next lunge.
cues: Back knee hovers just above floor
why: Combines hip extension and trunk rotation, like your body position on a shot.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
summary: Lunge, elbow to instep, rotate to the sky.
steps: Step into a deep lunge, hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Drop the inside elbow toward the instep.
Rotate that arm up to the ceiling, eyes follow the hand.
Hands down, straighten front leg for a hamstring stretch, then switch.
cues: Back leg stays straight and active
why: One move that hits every joint a skater locks up: hips, T-spine and hamstrings.

name: Arm Circles
summary: Small to big circles, both directions.
steps: Arms out to the side at shoulder height.
Make small circles, gradually getting bigger.
Reverse direction halfway.
why: Warms the shoulders for shooting, checking and stick work.

name: Inchworm
summary: Walk hands out to plank and back.
steps: Stand tall, hinge and put your hands on the floor.
Walk hands out to a plank.
Walk feet up toward your hands, keeping legs as straight as you can.
why: Warms up the hamstrings and core together.

name: Lateral Shuffle
summary: Athletic stance, shuffle side to side.
steps: Drop into an athletic stance, hips back, chest up.
Shuffle 3–4 steps one way, then back.
Keep feet from clicking together.
why: Same lateral push pattern as a skating stride.

name: Gate Openers
summary: Lift the knee and open the hip out to the side.
steps: Stand tall, lift one knee to hip height.
Rotate the knee out to the side, opening the hip.
Lower and repeat. Then reverse: out to in (gate closers).
cues: Don't lean away from the moving leg
why: Hockey hips live in external rotation. This loosens them before you load.

name: Band Pull-Apart
summary: Pull a band apart at chest height.
steps: Hold a band at shoulder width, arms straight in front.
Pull it apart until it touches your chest.
Return slowly.
cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
why: Offsets the hunched-over skating posture and protects the shoulders.

name: A-Skips
summary: Rhythmic skip with high knee drive.
steps: Skip forward, driving one knee to hip height.
Strike the ground under your hip with the opposite foot.
Swing arms opposite to legs.
cues: Toes up on the driving leg
why: Teaches crisp, stiff ground contact that carries over to quicker crossovers.

name: Goblet Squat
summary: Squat holding a dumbbell at your chest.
steps: Hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest.
Feet just wider than hips, toes slightly out.
Sit down between your heels until elbows touch knees.
Drive the floor away to stand.
why: Builds the quads and glutes that hold a low skating stance through a whole shift.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
summary: Rear foot elevated single-leg squat.
steps: Put the top of your back foot on a bench.
Front foot about two feet ahead.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
cues: Front knee stays stable, no caving
why: Skating is single-leg. This is the king of single-leg strength. Hold dumbbells to progress.

name: Reverse Lunge
summary: Step back into a lunge.
steps: Stand tall, step one foot back.
Lower until both knees are around 90°.
Push through the front foot to return.
why: Knee-friendly single-leg strength. Add dumbbells when it gets easy.

name: Side Lunge
summary: Big step to the side and sit into that hip.
steps: Feet together, take a wide step to the side.
Sit your hips back over the stepping leg, other leg straight.
Push back to the start.
why: Strengthens the groin through range: the exact position of a wide skating push.

name: Cossack Squat
summary: Deep side squat with the straight leg's toes up.
steps: Stand in a very wide stance.
Squat deep to one side, the other leg straight with toes pointing up.
Stay low and shift to the other side, or stand between reps.
cues: Heel of the bent leg stays down
Hold something for balance at first
why: Huge for groin strength and hip mobility at the same time.

name: Single-Leg RDL
summary: Hinge on one leg, the other leg reaches back.
steps: Hold a dumbbell in the hand opposite the standing leg.
Hinge at the hip, free leg reaches straight back.
Lower until your torso is near parallel.
Squeeze the glute to stand.
cues: Hips stay square to the floor
Soft knee on the standing leg
why: Builds the hamstrings and glutes that finish every stride, plus balance.

name: Dumbbell RDL
summary: Hip hinge with dumbbells.
steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Push your hips back, sliding the weights down your legs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive hips forward to stand.
cues: Weights stay close to your legs
why: Posterior chain strength for a powerful stride and hamstring injury resistance.

name: Glute Bridge
summary: Lie on your back and drive hips up.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Drive through your heels, lifting hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze and hold for one second, lower slowly.
cues: Ribs down, don't arch the lower back
why: Wakes up the glutes, which sit idle when you're hunched over all day.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
summary: Shoulders on a bench, drive up on one leg.
steps: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted, other knee pulled in.
Drive hips up until level.
Lower with control.
why: Single-leg hip extension is the engine of skating speed.

name: Wall Sit
summary: Hold a seated position against a wall.
steps: Back flat on a wall, slide down until thighs are parallel.
Knees at 90°, over the ankles.
Hold. Hands off your thighs.
why: Mimics the burn of holding a deep skating stance late in a shift.

name: Step-Ups
summary: Step onto a box, drive the knee up.
steps: Put one foot on a knee-height box.
Drive through that foot to stand on the box.
Lift the other knee up high.
Step down with control.
cues: Don't push off the back foot
Stand fully tall at the top
why: Single-leg drive that carries straight into explosive starts.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
summary: Kneel and lower your body forward slowly.
steps: Kneel with your ankles anchored under a couch or by a partner.
Keep your body straight from knees to head.
Lower forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands, push back up.
cues: Hips stay extended, don't bend at the waist
Fight it all the way down
why: Proven to slash hamstring strain rates. Worth doing year-round.

name: Copenhagen Plank
summary: Side plank with the top leg on a bench.
steps: Lie on your side, forearm on the floor.
Place your top leg on a bench (inside of knee for easier, ankle for harder).
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line, bottom leg hangs.
Hold.
cues: Squeeze the top leg down into the bench
why: The number one exercise for preventing groin strains in hockey players.

name: Skater Squat
summary: Single-leg squat, back knee touches down behind you.
steps: Stand on one leg, other knee bent with foot behind you.
Reach arms forward and squat down.
Lightly touch the back knee to a pad on the floor.
Stand back up without the back foot touching.
cues: Use a pad or pillow for your knee
why: Pure single-leg strength in a skating-specific position.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
summary: Rise up onto the ball of one foot.
steps: Stand on one foot on a step edge, heel hanging.
Rise as high as you can.
Lower slowly below the step.
why: Ankle stiffness and the last push of the stride through the toe.

name: Kettlebell Swing
summary: Explosive hip hinge swinging a kettlebell.
steps: Hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to float it to chest height.
Let it fall and hinge again.
cues: It's a hinge, not a squat
Glutes do the work, arms are ropes
why: Trains explosive hip extension and grip together.

name: Barbell Back Squat
summary: Heavy squat with a barbell on your upper back.
steps: Bar on your upper back, feet shoulder width.
Brace hard, sit down between your heels.
Hit parallel or below.
Drive up, keeping chest and hips rising together.
cues: Big breath and brace before each rep
why: Max strength is the foundation for every other quality: speed, power and durability.

name: Deadlift
summary: Lift a loaded bar from the floor.
steps: Bar over mid-foot, hinge and grab it.
Pull your chest up and lats tight.
Push the floor away until you're standing tall.
Lower under control.
why: Total-body strength for winning battles along the boards.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
summary: Side steps with a band around your knees or ankles.
steps: Band around knees or ankles, quarter squat.
Step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Go 12 steps, then come back.
why: Glute med strength keeps your knees stable on hard cuts.

name: Push-up
summary: The original. Chest to the floor, full lockout.
steps: Hands just wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower until your chest is an inch from the floor.
Press back up to full lockout.
why: Upper-body pushing strength for battles and protecting the puck.

name: Pull-up
summary: Hang and pull your chin over the bar.
steps: Hang with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your elbows down to your ribs.
Chin over the bar, lower all the way.
cues: Start each rep from a dead hang
why: Lat and grip strength for shooting power and stick control.

name: Inverted Row
summary: Row your body up to a low bar or sturdy table.
steps: Lie under a sturdy table or low bar, grip the edge.
Body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest up to the edge.
Lower slowly.
cues: Squeeze shoulder blades together at the top
why: Balances out all the pushing and builds the upper back for posture.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
summary: Press dumbbells from your chest on a bench.
steps: Lie on a bench with dumbbells at chest level.
Press up until arms are straight.
Lower until elbows are just below the bench.
why: Pushing strength to win net-front battles.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
summary: Row a dumbbell to your hip, one hand on a bench.
steps: One hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip.
Lower to a full stretch.
why: Strong lats are the hidden engine of a hard slap shot.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
summary: Press dumbbells overhead.
steps: Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms in.
Press straight up until arms are locked.
Lower back to shoulders.
why: Shoulder strength and stability for contact.

name: Band Face Pull
summary: Pull a band to your face, elbows high.
steps: Anchor a band at face height.
Pull it toward your forehead, splitting the hands apart.
Finish with elbows high and hands by your ears.
Return slowly.
cues: Thumbs point back at the end
why: Shoulder health insurance for a sport full of falls and collisions.

name: Tricep Dips
summary: Dip off the edge of a bench.
steps: Hands on the bench edge behind you, legs out.
Bend your elbows to lower your hips.
Press back up.
why: Triceps power behind your shot follow-through.

name: Farmer's Carry
summary: Walk carrying heavy weights at your sides.
steps: Pick up heavy dumbbells.
Walk tall with short, quick steps.
Keep going for the full time.
why: Grip strength translates directly to stick control and harder shots.

name: Wrist Curls
summary: Curl a dumbbell with just your wrist.
steps: Forearm on your thigh, wrist hanging off the knee.
Let the dumbbell roll to your fingers.
Curl it up with your wrist. Do palms up and palms down sets.
why: Wrist strength is the difference between a snap shot and a hard snap shot.

name: Pike Push-up
summary: Push-up with hips high to load the shoulders.
steps: Hips high in an upside-down V.
Lower your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up.
cues: Head goes forward of the hands
Keep legs as straight as you can
why: Bodyweight overhead strength when there's no gym around.

name: Renegade Row
summary: Plank on dumbbells and row one side at a time.
steps: High plank holding two dumbbells, feet wide.
Row one dumbbell to your hip.
Place it down and row the other.
why: Pulling strength while resisting rotation, like protecting the puck.

name: Band Row
summary: Row a band anchored in front of you.
steps: Anchor a band at chest height.
Step back for tension.
Pull hands to your ribs and squeeze.
why: Easy upper-back volume for posture.

name: Plyo Push-up
summary: Push so hard your hands leave the floor.
steps: Push-up position.
Lower under control.
Explode up so your hands leave the ground.
Land softly and go again.
why: Upper-body rate of force: think shoving a forechecker off the puck.

name: Plank
summary: Forearms down, body straight as a stick.
steps: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace and hold.
why: Core stiffness transfers leg power to your stick and your shot.

name: Side Plank
summary: Plank on your side, hips stacked.
steps: Lie on your side, elbow under shoulder.
Lift hips so your body is straight.
Hold, then switch sides.
cues: Top hand on hip or reaching up
why: Lateral stability for taking hits and leaning on edges.

name: Dead Bug
summary: On your back, extend opposite arm and leg.
steps: Lie on your back, arms up, knees over hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Return and switch.
why: Teaches the core to stay solid while the limbs move, like skating with the puck.

name: Pallof Press
summary: Press a band straight out and resist the twist.
steps: Anchor a band at chest height, stand side-on.
Hold it at your chest, step out for tension.
Press straight out and hold 2 seconds.
Bring it back in.
cues: Don't let it pull you around
why: Anti-rotation strength: what keeps you upright when you get bumped.

name: Russian Twist
summary: Seated rotation side to side.
steps: Sit, lean back slightly, feet up or down.
Rotate your torso to tap the floor on each side.
Hold a weight or med ball to progress.
cues: Rotate the shoulders, not just the arms
why: Rotational endurance for shooting and stickhandling.

name: Hollow Hold
summary: On your back, shoulders and legs hovering.
steps: Lie on your back, lower back pressed down.
Lift shoulders and legs off the floor, arms overhead.
Hold the banana shape.
cues: Bend the knees to make it easier
why: Builds the deep front-core strength under every athletic movement.

name: Bird Dog
summary: On all fours, reach opposite arm and leg.
steps: On hands and knees.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Hold 2 seconds, return, switch.
cues: Back stays flat like a table
why: Spine-friendly back strength. Great for players with tight, achy lower backs.

name: Mountain Climbers
summary: Plank and drive knees in fast.
steps: High plank.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch fast.
Keep hips level.
why: Core under fatigue with a skating-style knee drive.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
summary: Hang from a bar and lift your knees up.
steps: Hang from a bar.
Curl your knees toward your chest, tilting the pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.
cues: Curl the hips, don't just lift knees
why: Strong lower abs plus grip in one move.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
summary: High plank, tap opposite shoulders.
steps: High plank, feet a little wide.
Tap one hand to the opposite shoulder.
Alternate without rocking your hips.
why: Anti-rotation stability for contact.

name: V-Ups
summary: Fold up, hands meet feet.
steps: Lie flat, arms overhead.
Lift legs and torso together, reach hands to toes.
Lower slowly.
why: Explosive trunk flexion for shooting and battles.

name: Suitcase Carry
summary: Walk with a heavy weight in one hand.
steps: Hold a heavy dumbbell in one hand.
Walk tall without leaning.
Switch hands.
why: Lateral core strength and grip, like holding off a player with one arm.

name: Bear Crawl
summary: Crawl on hands and feet, knees just off the floor.
steps: On all fours, lift knees an inch off the floor.
Crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot.
Go forward and back.
why: Total core and shoulder stability with coordination.

name: Rotational Med Ball Throw
summary: Side-on to a wall, rotate and throw hard.
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, ball at your back hip.
Load the back hip, then rotate fast through the hips.
Throw the ball into the wall, catch and repeat.
cues: Hips start the rotation, arms finish
why: The closest gym movement to a slap shot. Builds rotational power.

name: Box Jump
summary: Jump up onto a box and land soft.
steps: Stand a foot from the box.
Swing your arms and load your hips.
Explode up, land softly on the box in a quarter squat.
Step down, don't jump down.
why: Raw lower-body power for your first three strides.

name: Squat Jump
summary: Squat and explode straight up.
steps: Squat to about parallel.
Explode up as high as you can.
Land soft and sink straight into the next rep.
cues: Full hip extension in the air
why: Basic power development for acceleration.

name: Broad Jump
summary: Jump forward as far as you can.
steps: Feet hip width, arms back.
Swing arms forward and jump out as far as you can.
Stick the landing for 2 seconds. Walk back.
why: Horizontal power. Strongly tied to on-ice sprint speed.

name: Lateral Skater Bound
summary: Leap side to side, landing on one leg.
steps: Stand on one leg in a skating stance.
Push off and bound sideways, landing on the other leg.
Stick the landing for a beat, then bound back.
why: The most hockey-specific power exercise there is. It's literally a stride.

name: Tuck Jump
summary: Jump and pull your knees to your chest.
steps: Stand tall, quarter squat.
Jump and pull your knees up toward your chest.
Land on the balls of your feet and rebound.
why: Reactive power and quick ground contact.

name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop
summary: Hop side to side over a line on one foot.
steps: Stand on one foot next to a line.
Hop over the line and back as quickly as you can.
Stay on the same foot the whole set.
why: Ankle and knee stability for quick edge changes.

name: Med Ball Slam
summary: Lift the ball overhead and slam it down.
steps: Hold a med ball, rise onto your toes and reach overhead.
Slam the ball into the floor as hard as you can.
Pick it up and repeat.
why: Total-body power and a great stress outlet.

name: Jump Lunges
summary: Lunge, explode up, switch legs mid-air.
steps: Start in a lunge.
Jump up and switch legs in the air.
Land softly in the opposite lunge.
why: Single-leg reactive power for starts and stops.

name: Pogo Hops
summary: Quick, stiff-ankle bounces.
steps: Stand tall, hands on hips.
Bounce on the balls of your feet using mostly your ankles.
Keep it quick and springy.
cues: Bounce off the ground like it's hot
why: Builds springy ankles and Achilles stiffness for explosive pushes.

name: Heiden Jumps
summary: Max-distance skater bound with a 2-second hold.
steps: Deep skating stance on one leg.
Explode sideways as far as you can.
Land on the opposite leg and hold perfectly still for 2 seconds.
Bound back.
why: Named after the speed skater. Builds stride power and the control to use it.

name: Lateral Shuffle Sprint
summary: Fast low shuffles between two markers.
steps: Place two markers 5 m apart.
In a low stance, shuffle as fast as you can between them.
Touch the marker each time.
why: Defensive gap control and lateral quickness.

name: Crossover Run
summary: Carioca: side step crossing in front and behind.
steps: Move sideways, crossing the trail leg in front.
Then step out and cross it behind.
Hips rotate, shoulders stay square.
why: Builds the hip rotation behind fast crossovers.

name: 10 m Sprint Starts
summary: Explode for 10 m, walk back, repeat.
steps: Start in a staggered athletic stance.
Explode forward for 10 m.
Walk back for recovery. Full effort every rep.
cues: Low and forward for the first 3 steps
why: Acceleration wins races to loose pucks. First step is everything.

name: T-Drill
summary: Sprint, shuffle left, shuffle right, backpedal.
steps: Set cones in a T: 10 yd forward, 5 yd each side.
Sprint to the middle cone.
Shuffle left, shuffle right across, shuffle back to the middle.
Backpedal to the start.
why: Forward, lateral and backward movement in one drill, like real play.

name: 5-10-5 Shuttle
summary: The NHL combine change-of-direction test.
steps: Three cones 5 yd apart, start at the middle.
Sprint 5 yd right, touch the line.
Sprint 10 yd left, touch the line.
Sprint 5 yd back through the middle.
cues: Plant hard on the outside foot
Drop the hips into each turn
why: Change of direction speed. Also one of your benchmarks.

name: Backpedal to Sprint
summary: Backpedal, then open the hips and sprint.
steps: Backpedal for 5 m in a low stance.
Open your hips and turn to sprint forward 10 m.
Walk back to recover.
why: Defenders: this is your pivot. Forwards: it's your backcheck turn.

name: Quick Feet
summary: Rapid tiny steps in place.
steps: Athletic stance.
Patter your feet as fast as possible.
On a clap (or every 5 s), sprint 3 steps and return.
cues: Stay on the balls of your feet
why: Foot speed and reaction for quick pivots.

name: Lateral Bound to Sprint
summary: Two skater bounds, then sprint forward.
steps: Do two big lateral skater bounds.
On landing, sprint forward 10 m.
Walk back, alternate starting side.
cues: No pause between bound and sprint
why: Lateral-to-linear transition, like a crossover start.

name: Burpees
summary: Squat, kick back, push-up, jump.
steps: Drop your hands to the floor and kick your feet back.
Do a push-up.
Jump your feet back to your hands.
Explode up into a jump.
why: Brutal full-body conditioning that teaches you to get up off the ice fast.

name: Shift Sprints
summary: Hard 40-second efforts with long rest, like real shifts.
steps: Pick a mode: sprint, bike, stairs, jump rope or skater hops.
Go hard for the full time.
Rest while the timer runs down, just like the bench.
cues: Hold the same pace every round
Breathe through the nose on rest
why: Trains the exact energy system of a hockey shift: short, hard, repeat.

name: Skater Hops
summary: Continuous quick side-to-side skater jumps.
steps: Hop side to side from one leg to the other.
Keep a fast, steady rhythm.
Swing the arms across like a skater.
why: Stride-specific conditioning that burns like a long shift.

name: Jump Rope
summary: Skip rope at a steady pace.
steps: Hold handles at hip height.
Turn the rope with your wrists.
Small hops on the balls of your feet.
why: Footwork, rhythm and aerobic base at the same time.

name: Sprawls
summary: Drop to the floor and pop back up, fast.
steps: Drop hands down and shoot your feet back, hips to the floor.
Snap your feet back under you.
Stand and repeat.
why: Getting up quickly after going down. Shift-length intensity.

name: Slide Board
summary: Slide side to side in a full skating stride.
steps: Booties on, stand on one end in a skating stance.
Push off and glide to the other end.
Absorb with the outside leg and push back.
cues: Full leg extension on each push
Stay low and quiet up top
why: Off-ice skating. Conditioning and stride mechanics together.

name: Tempo Run
summary: Run at about 70% for a minute, walk to recover.
steps: Run at a comfortable but quick pace.
Walk back during rest.
Keep every rep the same speed.
why: Aerobic base helps you recover between shifts and between periods.

name: Squat Thrust to Tuck
summary: Squat thrust finished with a tuck jump.
steps: Hands down, kick feet back.
Jump feet back in.
Explode into a tuck jump.
why: High-intensity conditioning with a power finish.

name: Single-Leg Star Reach
summary: Balance on one leg, tap the other foot in all directions.
steps: Stand on one leg, slight bend in the knee.
Reach the free foot forward, to the side and behind, tapping lightly.
Don't put weight on the reaching foot.
cues: Standing knee stays over the toes
Reach as far as you can control
why: Knee and ankle control for edge work and staying on your feet.

name: Hop and Stick
summary: Hop forward on one leg and freeze.
steps: Stand on one leg.
Hop forward a short distance.
Land and hold perfectly still for 3 seconds.
why: Landing control protects your ACL and ankles.

name: Eyes-Closed Single-Leg Stand
summary: Balance on one leg with your eyes shut.
steps: Stand on one leg near a wall.
Close your eyes.
Hold steady. Touch down if needed and restart.
cues: Grip the floor with your toes
why: Trains proprioception, the sense skaters rely on when eyes are on the play.

name: Single-Leg Squat to Reach
summary: Single-leg quarter squat reaching hands to the floor.
steps: Stand on one leg.
Squat partway and reach both hands toward the floor in front.
Stand tall again.
why: Builds stable single-leg strength in a stride-like position.

name: 90/90 Hip Switch
summary: Seated, rotate knees side to side.
steps: Sit with both knees bent at 90°, one in front and one to the side.
Rotate both knees over to the other side.
Sit tall, lean forward over the front shin for a stretch.
cues: Use your hands behind you at first
why: Internal and external hip rotation: the range hockey players lose first.

name: Couch Stretch
summary: Kneeling quad and hip-flexor stretch with foot up a wall.
steps: Kneel with your back knee against a wall or couch, shin up it.
Front foot planted in a lunge.
Squeeze the back glute and sit tall.
why: Undoes hours of skating in a flexed hip position.

name: Frog Stretch
summary: On all fours, knees wide, sink the hips back.
steps: On hands and knees, slide your knees out wide.
Ankles in line with knees.
Gently rock your hips back.
why: Groin flexibility, the area that takes the most abuse in hockey.

name: Pigeon Stretch
summary: Front shin across, back leg straight.
steps: From a plank, bring one knee forward behind your wrist.
Lay the shin across and extend the back leg.
Sink down and breathe.
cues: Prop yourself up on a pillow if needed
why: Relieves tight glutes and the lower back pain that comes with them.

name: Thoracic Open Book
summary: Side-lying chest rotation.
steps: Lie on your side, knees bent to 90°, arms straight in front.
Open the top arm up and over to the other side.
Follow your hand with your eyes, then return.
why: Upper-back rotation for shooting and looking over your shoulder.

name: Deep Squat Hold
summary: Sit in the bottom of a squat.
steps: Sink into your deepest squat, heels down.
Push knees out with your elbows.
Sit tall and breathe.
cues: Hold something if you tip back
why: Ankle, hip and groin mobility in one position.

name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
summary: On your back, pull a straight leg up.
steps: Lie on your back, band or towel around one foot.
Keep the leg straight and pull it up.
Other leg stays flat on the floor.
why: Hamstrings tighten up from the skating crouch.

name: Cat-Cow
summary: On all fours, round and arch your spine.
steps: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Round your back to the ceiling, chin tucked.
Arch and look up. Move slowly with your breath.
cues: Move one vertebra at a time
why: Keeps the spine moving after long periods hunched in a stance.

name: Adductor Rock-Back
summary: One leg out to the side, rock hips back.
steps: On all fours, extend one leg straight out to the side.
Rock your hips back toward your heel.
Return and repeat.
why: Dynamic groin mobility. Great pre-game.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
summary: Half-kneel and push your hips forward.
steps: Half-kneeling, front knee at 90°.
Tuck your tailbone and squeeze the back glute.
Shift forward slightly, reach the same-side arm up.
why: Tight hip flexors steal stride length.

name: Child's Pose
summary: Kneel, sit back, reach forward.
steps: Kneel and sit back on your heels.
Reach your arms forward on the floor.
Breathe slowly into your back.
why: Downshifts your nervous system after training.

name: Foam Roll: Quads & IT
summary: Roll the fronts and outsides of the thighs.
steps: Lie face down with the roller under your thighs.
Roll from hip to just above the knee.
Pause on tight spots for 10 seconds. Turn to the sides.
why: Quads take a beating from the skating stance. Helps you recover.

name: Foam Roll: Upper Back
summary: Roll the upper back and lats.
steps: Roller under your upper back, hands behind your head.
Lift your hips and roll from mid-back to shoulders.
Lean to each side for the lats.
why: Loosens up the hunched posture from skating.

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Mobility
summary: Drive the knee over the toes to a wall.
steps: Half-kneel facing a wall, front toes a few inches away.
Drive your knee forward to touch the wall.
Keep the heel down. Move the foot back as you improve.
cues: Knee tracks over the middle toes
why: Skates lock your ankles. Good ankle range means deeper knee bend.

name: Lying Hip Internal Rotation
summary: On your back, drop one knee inward.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet wide.
Let one knee drop in toward the floor.
Put the other foot on top of that knee for extra stretch.
why: Goalies and skaters both lose internal rotation. This gets it back.

name: Figure 8 Dribble
summary: Stickhandle in a figure 8 around two objects.
steps: Place two objects (pucks, cones, shoes) a stick-length apart.
Stickhandle the ball in a figure 8 around them.
Change direction every 15 seconds.
why: Builds control on both forehand and backhand around defenders' sticks.

name: Wide-Narrow Dribble
summary: Alternate wide and tight stickhandling.
steps: Stickhandle wide, past your shoulders.
Switch to a tight, fast dribble in front of you.
Alternate every 5 seconds.
why: Changes of pace with the puck beat defenders.

name: Toe Drags
summary: Pull the ball across with the toe of the blade.
steps: Push the ball out to your forehand side.
Roll your wrists to cup the ball with the toe.
Drag it across your body. Repeat to the other side with a backhand pull.
why: The dangle move. Pulls the puck around a poke check.

name: One-Hand Stickhandling
summary: Stickhandle with just your top hand.
steps: Hold the stick with your top hand only.
Stickhandle in front of you.
Switch to bottom hand only for the second side.
why: Top-hand control is the base of soft hands. Bottom hand builds strength.

name: Heads-Up Stickhandling
summary: Stickhandle while reading something across the room.
steps: Pick a point on the wall or have a TV on.
Stickhandle without looking down.
Read numbers, signs, or count your fingers held up.
why: Eyes up = seeing passing lanes and open teammates.

name: Obstacle Weave
summary: Weave through a line of objects and back.
steps: Set 4–6 objects in a line, about 3 feet apart.
Weave through, moving your feet.
Come back using your backhand.
why: Stickhandling while moving, which is how you actually play.

name: Quick Hands
summary: Tiny, as-fast-as-possible dribble.
steps: Stickhandle in a 6-inch window.
Go as fast as you can while keeping control.
Count touches and try to beat it next time.
why: Hand speed for tight spaces and quick moves in traffic.

name: Between-the-Legs Pull
summary: Pull the ball back through your legs and recover.
steps: Wide stance with the ball on your forehand.
Pull it back between your legs.
Reach behind and bring it back out front on your forehand.
why: Flashy, but it builds stick reach and coordination nothing else does.

name: Wrist Shots
summary: Sweep and roll through the puck.
steps: Puck at the heel of the blade, beside your back foot.
Sweep forward, transferring weight to your front foot.
Roll the wrists and point the toe of the blade at your target.
cues: Follow through low for low shots
why: The most-used shot in hockey. Reps build accuracy.

name: Snap Shots
summary: Short backswing, flex and snap.
steps: Short backswing a foot behind the puck.
Strike the ice just behind the puck to flex the stick.
Snap the wrists through with a short follow-through.
why: Shoot before the goalie sets. Release speed scores goals.

name: Slap Shots
summary: Full wind-up, strike behind the puck.
steps: Puck between your feet, slightly forward.
Wind up with the stick to shoulder height.
Strike the surface 2 inches behind the puck.
Transfer weight and follow through at the target.
cues: Bottom hand low on the stick
why: Power from the point. Rotational strength pays off here.

name: Backhand Shots
summary: Sweep and lift on the backhand.
steps: Puck on the backhand side, near the heel.
Sweep across your body, shifting weight.
Lift through with your bottom hand and follow through high.
cues: Look at the target, then the puck
why: The most underrated shot. Goalies hate it.

name: Catch & Release
summary: Receive a pass off a board and shoot in one motion.
steps: Bank the ball off a rebounder, wall or have it fed.
Cushion it into the shooting pocket.
Release immediately without an extra touch.
cues: Feet set before the puck arrives
why: Catch-and-shoot is how most goals are scored off a pass.

name: Butterfly Drops
summary: Drop into a butterfly and recover to stance.
steps: Start in your goalie stance.
Drop to your knees in a butterfly, knees together, feet out.
Recover one leg at a time back to stance.
cues: Use a soft surface or knee pads
why: Builds the strength to drop and recover all game long.

name: T-Push Lateral
summary: Explosive lateral pushes in stance.
steps: In stance, turn your lead foot toward the push direction.
Push hard off the back leg and travel 2–3 m.
Stop square and set. Push back.
cues: Head leads, eyes on a target
why: Lateral power for crease movement.

name: Wall Ball Reactions
summary: Throw a tennis ball at a wall and catch it.
steps: Stand 6–8 feet from a wall in stance.
Throw a tennis ball and catch it on the rebound.
Alternate hands. Move closer or throw harder to progress.
cues: Track the ball all the way in
why: Hand-eye coordination and reaction time.

name: Goalie Hip Rotations
summary: Kneeling internal rotation lifts.
steps: Kneel tall on both knees.
Lift one foot out to the side by rotating the hip.
Hold 1 second at the top and lower.
why: Goalies need extreme hip internal rotation. This builds it with strength.

name: Shuffle to Butterfly
summary: Two quick shuffles, drop to butterfly, recover.
steps: Shuffle two steps in stance.
Drop into a butterfly.
Recover and shuffle back the other way.
why: Combines lateral movement with the save position.

name: Warm-up Jog
summary: Easy jog to raise your temperature.
steps: Jog at an easy, conversational pace.
Loosen your shoulders and arms.
Pick it up slightly at the end.
why: Raises body temperature so everything after feels better.

name: Butt Kickers
summary: Jog forward, heels kicking up to your glutes.
steps: Jog forward slowly.
Kick your heels up to touch your glutes.
Quick turnover, arms pumping.
why: Loosens the quads and warms up the hamstrings.

name: Walking Knee Hugs
summary: Step, pull one knee to your chest, rise on your toes.
steps: Step forward and pull the opposite knee to your chest.
Rise up on the toes of the standing foot.
Release and repeat on the other side.
why: Opens up the glutes and lower back while working balance.

name: Walking Quad Pull
summary: Step, grab your ankle and pull the heel to your glute.
steps: Step forward and grab the back ankle.
Pull the heel to your glute and reach the other arm up.
Release, step and switch.
why: Dynamic quad and hip-flexor stretch.

name: Frankenstein Walk
summary: Kick a straight leg up to your opposite hand.
steps: Walk forward with one arm straight out.
Kick the opposite straight leg up toward your hand.
Alternate each step.
why: Also called toy soldiers. Dynamic hamstring stretch.

name: Carioca
summary: Grapevine sideways, crossing in front and behind.
steps: Move sideways.
Cross the trailing leg in front, then step out, then cross behind.
Rotate the hips, keep shoulders square. Go both directions.
why: Hip rotation and footwork.

name: Backpedal
summary: Run backward in a low stance.
steps: Get low, weight on the balls of your feet.
Push yourself backward with quick steps.
Stay low the whole way.
why: Wakes up the quads and coordination.

name: Spiderman Lunge
summary: Lunge forward, drop the elbow inside the foot.
steps: Step into a deep lunge.
Place both hands down and drop the inside elbow toward the instep.
Step through into the next one.
why: Deep hip and groin opener.

name: Power Skips
summary: Skip for maximum height.
steps: Skip forward, driving one knee up hard.
Swing the opposite arm high.
Go for height, not distance.
why: Primes explosiveness before hard work.

name: B-Skips
summary: A-skip with a leg extension and paw back.
steps: Skip and drive the knee up.
Extend the leg out in front.
Paw it back down under your hip.
why: Sprint mechanics drill.

name: Side Skips
summary: Skip sideways with arms swinging overhead.
steps: Turn sideways and skip.
Swing your arms up and down like jumping jacks.
Switch direction.
why: Warms up the hips and shoulders together.

name: Hip Cradle Walk
summary: Lift your shin and cradle it to your chest.
steps: Step forward and lift the opposite leg.
Hold the knee and ankle and pull the shin across your chest.
Release and step.
why: Opens the outer hip.

name: Heel & Toe Walks
summary: Walk on your heels, then on your toes.
steps: Walk 10 steps on your heels with toes up.
Walk 10 steps on your toes.
Repeat.
why: Wakes up the ankles and shins.

name: Lunge with Overhead Reach
summary: Walking lunge, reach both arms up and lean.
steps: Step into a lunge.
Reach both arms overhead and lean away from the front leg.
Step through.
why: Hip-flexor and side-body opener.

name: Easy Run
summary: Steady, conversational pace.
steps: Run at a pace where you could hold a conversation.
Relax your shoulders and keep a quick cadence.
Stay steady the whole time.
why: Builds your aerobic base so you recover faster between efforts.

name: 100 m Strides
summary: Build to about 85% speed over 100 m.
steps: Start easy and build speed over the first 60 m.
Hold smooth, fast running for the last 40 m.
Walk back to recover.
why: Teaches efficient fast running without much fatigue.

name: 200 m Repeats
summary: Hard 200s with recovery.
steps: Run 200 m at about 90% effort.
Walk or jog easy during the rest.
Keep every rep the same speed.
why: Speed endurance: repeat hard efforts like long shifts.

name: 400 m Repeats
summary: One lap hard, recover, repeat.
steps: Run 400 m at a hard but controlled pace.
Recover for the rest period.
Match your time each rep.
why: Boosts VO2 max and lactate tolerance.

name: Tempo Kilometer
summary: Comfortably hard 1 km repeats.
steps: Run 1 km at a comfortably hard pace.
Recover with easy jogging.
Repeat.
cues: You can speak a few words, not sentences
why: Raises the pace you can hold before you fade.

name: Mile Run
summary: One continuous mile. Time it.
steps: Warm up first.
Run 1600 m at your best sustainable pace.
Note your time.
why: Classic fitness test and conditioning piece.

name: Fartlek Run
summary: Easy running mixed with random fast bursts.
steps: Run easy.
Every minute or so, surge hard for 10–30 seconds.
Return to easy and repeat.
why: Unpredictable bursts like real games.

name: Shuttle Runs
summary: Sprint between two lines, touching each.
steps: Set two markers 10–20 m apart.
Sprint, touch the line, turn and sprint back.
Each length is one rep.
why: Acceleration, deceleration and conditioning.

name: Distance Run
summary: Run a set distance at a steady pace.
steps: Warm up with a few minutes of easy jogging.
Run the full distance at a pace you can hold.
Note your time so you can beat it.
why: Builds the aerobic engine that helps you recover between shifts.

name: Free Stickhandling
summary: Open stickhandling time. Mix every move you know.
steps: Stay in a skating stance.
Cycle through wide-narrow, toe drags, figure 8s and one-hand work.
Keep your eyes up as much as possible.
why: Volume is what builds hands. Ten minutes a day adds up fast.

name: Cool-down Jog
summary: Very easy jog or brisk walk to bring the heart rate down.
steps: Jog or walk very easily.
Breathe slowly.
Shake out your legs and arms.
why: Helps you recover before stretching.

name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
summary: Heel forward, hinge over the straight leg.
steps: Put one heel forward, toes up, leg straight.
Bend the back knee and hinge forward.
Hold.
why: Hamstring stretch you can do anywhere.

name: Standing Side Reach
summary: Reach one arm overhead and lean.
steps: Stand tall, feet together.
Reach one arm overhead and lean to the side.
Hold, then switch.
why: Opens the side body and lats.

name: Standing Groin Stretch
summary: Wide stance, shift to one side.
steps: Take a wide stance.
Bend one knee and shift your weight over it.
Keep the other leg straight and hold.
why: Groin stretch without getting on the floor.

name: Standing Figure-4
summary: Ankle over knee, sit back on one leg.
steps: Stand on one leg, cross the other ankle over the knee.
Sit back like a chair.
Hold something for balance if needed.
why: Outer hip and glute release.

name: Bodyweight Squat
summary: The basic squat. No weight, full depth.
steps: Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Push hips back and bend knees until thighs are parallel or lower.
Drive through your whole foot to stand.
cues: Chest up, arms forward for balance
why: The foundation of every lower-body movement. Builds leg strength and mobility.

name: Sumo Squat
summary: Wide-stance squat, toes turned out.
steps: Stand with feet wide, toes pointed out 45°.
Sit straight down, knees pushing out over toes.
Squeeze glutes to stand.
cues: Hold a dumbbell between your legs to progress
why: Hits the inner thighs and glutes more than a regular squat.

name: Forward Lunge
summary: Step forward into a lunge and push back.
steps: Stand tall, take a big step forward.
Lower until both knees are at 90°.
Push off the front foot back to standing.
why: Builds single-leg strength, balance and deceleration.

name: Walking Lunges
summary: Lunge forward, step through, repeat.
steps: Step forward into a lunge.
Drive through the front foot and bring the back leg straight into the next lunge.
Keep travelling forward.
why: Leg strength and conditioning in one.

name: Curtsy Lunge
summary: Step back and across behind you.
steps: Stand tall, step one leg back and across behind the other.
Lower until the front thigh is near parallel.
Return to start.
why: Targets the side glutes that stabilise your knees.

name: Donkey Kicks
summary: On all fours, kick one foot up to the ceiling.
steps: Get on hands and knees.
Keeping the knee bent, lift one foot toward the ceiling.
Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.
cues: Squeeze the glute, not the back
why: Isolates the glutes. Great warm-up or burnout.

name: Fire Hydrants
summary: On all fours, lift the knee out to the side.
steps: Hands and knees, back flat.
Lift one knee out to the side, keeping it bent.
Lower slowly.
why: Strengthens the hip abductors that keep knees stable.

name: Calf Raises
summary: Rise onto your toes and lower.
steps: Stand tall, feet hip width.
Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet.
Lower slowly.
why: Stronger calves and ankles for running and jumping.

name: Squat Pulses
summary: Stay low and pulse up and down a few inches.
steps: Sink into a squat.
Pulse up and down 2–3 inches without standing.
Keep going for the full time.
why: A brutal quad burner with zero equipment.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
summary: Glute bridge with one leg in the air.
steps: Lie on your back, one foot planted, other leg straight up.
Drive hips up through the planted heel.
Lower slowly.
why: Fixes left/right glute imbalances.

name: Dumbbell Squat
summary: Squat holding dumbbells at your sides or shoulders.
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides or on your shoulders.
Squat to parallel.
Stand up strong.
why: Adds load to the basic squat for more strength.

name: Band Glute Kickback
summary: Kick one leg back against a band.
steps: Loop a band around your ankles, hold something for balance.
Kick one leg straight back.
Return slowly.
why: Glute isolation without heavy weight.

name: Knee Push-up
summary: Push-up from your knees. The easier version.
steps: Hands under shoulders, knees on the floor.
Body straight from knees to head.
Lower your chest to the floor and press up.
why: Builds the strength to do full push-ups.

name: Incline Push-up
summary: Push-up with your hands on a bench or counter.
steps: Hands on a bench, body straight.
Lower your chest to the edge.
Press back up.
why: Easier push-up variation that still builds strength.

name: Decline Push-up
summary: Push-up with your feet up on a bench.
steps: Feet on a bench, hands on the floor.
Lower your chest down.
Press back up.
why: Harder push-up that loads the upper chest and shoulders.

name: Wide Push-up
summary: Push-up with hands wider than shoulders.
steps: Hands wide, about 1.5× shoulder width.
Lower your chest between your hands.
Press back up.
why: More chest, less triceps.

name: Diamond Push-up
summary: Hands together under your chest.
steps: Make a diamond with your thumbs and index fingers under your chest.
Lower until your chest touches your hands.
Press up.
why: The hardest bodyweight triceps move.

name: Chin-up
summary: Pull-up with palms facing you.
steps: Hang with palms facing you, shoulder width.
Pull until your chin is over the bar.
Lower all the way.
why: Biceps and back strength. A bit easier than pull-ups.

name: Bicep Curl
summary: Curl dumbbells up to your shoulders.
steps: Dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl up, keeping elbows pinned.
Lower slowly.
why: Bigger, stronger arms.

name: Hammer Curl
summary: Curl with palms facing each other.
steps: Dumbbells at your sides, palms in.
Curl up keeping the palms facing in.
Lower slowly.
why: Hits the forearms and grip along with the biceps.

name: Lateral Raise
summary: Raise dumbbells out to the sides.
steps: Light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise them out to shoulder height, slight bend in the elbows.
Lower slowly.
why: Wider, stronger shoulders.

name: Front Raise
summary: Raise dumbbells straight in front.
steps: Dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise straight forward to shoulder height.
Lower slowly.
why: Front shoulder strength.

name: Arnold Press
summary: Rotating shoulder press.
steps: Dumbbells at chin height, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating palms to face forward.
Reverse on the way down.
why: Hits all three parts of the shoulder.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
summary: Lower a dumbbell behind your head and press up.
steps: Hold one dumbbell with both hands overhead.
Bend elbows to lower it behind your head.
Extend back up.
why: Builds the long head of the triceps.

name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
summary: Lying tricep extension.
steps: Lie on a bench, dumbbells straight up.
Bend elbows to lower them beside your head.
Extend back up.
why: Triceps strength for pushing.

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
summary: Open your arms wide and hug back up.
steps: Lie on a bench, dumbbells above your chest.
Open your arms wide with a slight elbow bend.
Squeeze them back together.
why: Isolates the chest.

name: Reverse Fly
summary: Bent over, raise dumbbells out to the sides.
steps: Hinge forward with light dumbbells hanging.
Raise them out to the sides.
Lower slowly.
why: Better posture, healthier shoulders.

name: Upright Row
summary: Pull dumbbells up to your chest.
steps: Dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Pull them up to chest height, elbows high.
Lower slowly.
why: Shoulders and traps in one move.

name: Superman
summary: Lying face down, lift arms and legs.
steps: Lie face down, arms straight ahead.
Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor.
Hold for 2 seconds and lower.
why: Strengthens the whole back side of your body.

name: Negative Pull-up
summary: Jump to the top and lower slowly.
steps: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself as slowly as you can.
Reset and repeat.
why: The fastest way to get your first pull-up.

name: Crunches
summary: Curl your shoulders off the floor.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands by your ears.
Curl your shoulders off the floor.
Lower slowly.
why: Classic ab builder.

name: Sit-ups
summary: Sit all the way up from lying down.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Sit all the way up.
Lower back down with control.
cues: Hook feet under something if needed
why: Full-range ab and hip-flexor strength.

name: Bicycle Crunches
summary: Elbow to opposite knee, pedalling.
steps: Lie on your back, hands by your head, legs up.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg.
Switch sides in a pedalling motion.
cues: Rotate the shoulder, not just the elbow
why: One of the best moves for obliques.

name: Flutter Kicks
summary: Legs straight, small fast kicks.
steps: Lie on your back, hands under your hips.
Lift your legs a few inches off the floor.
Kick them up and down in small, quick movements.
why: Lower-ab endurance.

name: Lying Leg Raise
summary: Raise straight legs to the ceiling.
steps: Lie flat, hands under your hips.
Lift straight legs until they point at the ceiling.
Lower slowly without touching the floor.
why: Strong lower abs.

name: Reverse Crunch
summary: Curl your hips up toward your chest.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent at 90° in the air.
Curl your hips off the floor toward your chest.
Lower slowly.
why: Lower abs without straining the neck.

name: Heel Touches
summary: Side to side, reaching for your heels.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, shoulders slightly lifted.
Reach one hand to the same-side heel.
Alternate sides.
why: Oblique burner.

name: Toe Touch Crunch
summary: Legs up, reach for your toes.
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight up.
Reach your hands up to your toes.
Lower your shoulders slowly.
why: Upper-ab focus.

name: Plank Jacks
summary: Jumping jacks with your feet in a plank.
steps: High plank.
Jump your feet wide, then back together.
Keep hips level.
why: Core plus cardio.

name: Side Plank Hip Dips
summary: Side plank, dip the hip and lift.
steps: Side plank on your forearm.
Lower your hip toward the floor.
Lift it back up high.
why: Obliques and side stability.

name: Windshield Wipers
summary: Legs up, rock them side to side.
steps: Lie on your back, arms out wide, legs straight up.
Lower your legs to one side.
Bring them back up and over to the other side.
cues: Bend knees to make it easier
why: Serious rotational core strength.

name: Scissor Kicks
summary: Cross your legs over each other.
steps: Lie on your back, legs lifted a few inches.
Cross one leg over the other, then switch.
Keep it going.
why: Lower abs and inner thighs.

name: Sit-up Twist
summary: Sit up and twist to one side.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent.
Sit up and rotate to bring an elbow across your knee.
Lower and alternate sides.
why: Abs and obliques together.

name: Butt Kicks
summary: Run in place, heels to your glutes.
steps: Jog in place.
Kick your heels up to touch your glutes.
Keep a quick pace.
cues: Stay on the balls of your feet
why: Warms up the hamstrings and gets the heart rate up.

name: Star Jumps
summary: Explode up into a star shape.
steps: Squat down a little.
Jump up, spreading your arms and legs into a star.
Land softly with feet together.
why: Explosive full-body cardio.

name: Squat Jacks
summary: Jumping jacks in a low squat.
steps: Get in a half squat, hands at your chest.
Jump feet out wide and back in, staying low.
Keep going.
why: Leg burn plus cardio.

name: Shadow Boxing
summary: Throw fast punches at nothing.
steps: Fighting stance, hands up.
Throw jabs, crosses and hooks.
Stay light on your feet.
why: Fun cardio that works shoulders and core.

name: Frog Jumps
summary: Deep squat, jump forward, land in a squat.
steps: Deep squat, hands touching the floor.
Jump forward as far as you can.
Land back in the squat and repeat.
why: Leg power and conditioning.

name: Run in Place
summary: Easy jog without going anywhere.
steps: Jog in place.
Pump your arms.
Pick up the pace for the last 10 seconds.
why: Simple cardio anywhere.

name: Half Burpees
summary: Burpee without the push-up and jump.
steps: Squat, put your hands down.
Jump your feet back to a plank.
Jump them back in and stand up.
why: Easier burpee that still gets your heart rate up.

name: Inchworm Push-up
summary: Walk out, push-up, walk back.
steps: Bend down and walk your hands out to a plank.
Do one push-up.
Walk your hands back and stand up.
why: Full-body: strength, mobility and cardio.

name: Jump Squat to Hold
summary: Jump squat, land and freeze for a second.
steps: Squat and jump as high as you can.
Land in a squat and hold for 1 second.
Go again.
why: Power with landing control.

name: Standing Quad Stretch
summary: Pull your heel to your glute.
steps: Stand on one leg, hold a wall if needed.
Grab your other ankle and pull your heel toward your glute.
Knees together, hold.
why: Loosens tight quads after leg work.

name: Standing Toe Touch
summary: Fold forward and reach for your toes.
steps: Feet together, knees soft.
Fold forward from your hips.
Let your head hang and reach for your toes.
why: Hamstring and lower-back release.

name: Cobra Stretch
summary: Lying face down, press your chest up.
steps: Lie face down, hands under your shoulders.
Press up, lifting your chest.
Keep hips on the floor and hold.
cues: Only go as high as is comfortable
why: Opens up the front of the body after sitting or crunches.

name: Butterfly Stretch
summary: Seated, soles together, knees down.
steps: Sit with the soles of your feet together.
Hold your feet and let your knees drop.
Lean forward gently.
why: Inner thigh and hip flexibility.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
summary: Forearm on a door frame, lean through.
steps: Place your forearm on a door frame, elbow at shoulder height.
Step through and turn away slightly.
Hold.
why: Undoes tight chest from push-ups and phones.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
summary: Pull one arm across your chest.
steps: Bring one arm across your chest.
Pull it in with the other arm.
Hold, then switch.
why: Rear shoulder release.

name: Overhead Tricep Stretch
summary: Hand behind your head, push the elbow.
steps: Reach one hand down behind your head.
Gently push the elbow with the other hand.
Hold, then switch.
why: Loosens triceps and lats.

name: Downward Dog
summary: Hips high, heels toward the floor.
steps: From a plank, push your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs, press heels down.
Push the floor away with your hands.
cues: Pedal your feet to loosen calves
why: Stretches the whole back of your body at once.

name: Lying Spinal Twist
summary: On your back, drop your knees to one side.
steps: Lie on your back, arms out wide.
Bring your knees up and drop them to one side.
Look the other way and breathe.
why: Releases a tight lower back.

name: Wall Calf Stretch
summary: Hands on a wall, back leg straight.
steps: Hands on a wall, one foot back.
Keep the back heel down and leg straight.
Lean in and hold.
why: Loose calves mean better ankles and fewer shin splints.

name: Neck Rolls
summary: Slow circles with your head.
steps: Sit or stand tall.
Slowly roll your head in a circle.
Switch directions halfway.
why: Eases neck tension.

name: Backhand Lifts
summary: Get the backhand off the ice and up under the bar.
steps: Puck on the backhand, near the heel, slightly behind your back foot.
Sweep forward and roll your bottom wrist under to open the blade.
Lift through with the bottom hand and finish with the blade pointing at the top corner.
cues: Cup the puck, don't slap it
why: A lifted backhand beats goalies in tight, and most players can't do it.

name: Shoot from the Middle
summary: Pull the puck to the middle of your body and release from there.
steps: Start with the puck out wide on your forehand.
Pull it across into the middle of your body, between your feet.
Release immediately from the middle without bringing it back to the side.
cues: Change the angle on the goalie
why: Changing the shooting angle right before you release freezes goalies and gets around defenders' sticks.

name: Around the Puck & Shoot
summary: Stickhandle around a puck or cone, then shoot in stride.
steps: Set a puck or cone a few feet in front of you.
Carry the ball around it (forehand side, then backhand side).
Come out of the turn and shoot without stopping.
cues: Head up coming out of the turn
why: Shooting right after a move is how goals happen in games.

name: Toe Drag & Shoot
summary: Toe drag around an obstacle, then snap it.
steps: Put a stick or object on the floor as a defender's stick.
Push the puck out, toe drag it back around the obstacle.
Snap a shot the moment it clears.
cues: Pull it tight to your feet
No extra touches before the shot
why: Beat the stick, beat the goalie. One fluid motion.

name: Corner Target Practice
summary: Call a corner before every shot.
steps: Hang targets in the corners or pick spots on the net.
Call your corner out loud, then shoot.
Count how many hit. Use the Aim Trainer for random calls.
why: Goalies cover the middle. Corners score.

name: Low Shots: Pad Side
summary: Keep every shot low, just off the ice, to the pads.
steps: Aim low glove and low blocker, 6 inches off the ice.
Keep your top hand forward and finish low.
Alternate sides.
why: Low shots create rebounds, and most goals come from rebounds.

name: Release in Your Feet
summary: Shoot with the puck in your feet, no wind-up.
steps: Puck in the middle of your stance.
Shoot immediately with almost no backswing.
Try it off the front foot and the back foot.
why: In traffic there's no time to load up.

name: Walk-In Shots
summary: Step into every shot like you're skating in.
steps: Start a few steps back.
Walk or skate in, carrying the puck.
Shoot in stride off your front foot.
why: Teaches you to shoot moving instead of standing still.

name: One-Timers
summary: Shoot a moving puck without stopping it.
steps: Bank passes off a rebounder or get fed passes.
Load early: stick back before the puck arrives.
Strike it as it reaches you, no catch.
why: The power-play weapon.

name: Saucer Passes
summary: Flip the puck so it lands flat over an obstacle.
steps: Put a stick on the ground as an obstacle.
Spin the puck off the toe of the blade so it flies flat.
Land it flat on the other side, at a wall or target.
why: Saucer passes beat sticks in the lane.

name: Forehand-Backhand Deke & Finish
summary: Fake forehand, pull to backhand, lift it.
steps: Approach the net with the puck on the forehand.
Fake the shot, pull hard to the backhand.
Lift it high on the backhand.
why: The breakaway move every goalie has to respect.

name: Rebound Finishes
summary: Shoot, then immediately bury the second puck.
steps: Put two pucks out.
Shoot the first, immediately grab and shoot the second.
Pretend the first one was saved.
cues: Quick hands for the second shot
why: Being ready for the rebound is half of scoring.

name: Around the Puck
summary: Stickhandle circles around a stationary puck or object.
steps: Set a puck down in front of you.
Stickhandle the ball in a circle around it, forehand side then backhand side.
Switch direction halfway.
cues: Keep the ball close to the puck
why: Teaches you to protect the puck around a stick or skate.

name: Puck Maze
summary: Weave through a field of scattered pucks.
steps: Scatter 6–10 pucks or objects randomly.
Weave through them without touching any.
Keep moving and change direction often.
why: Handling in traffic, like a crowded slot.

name: Toe Drag Around Obstacle
summary: Pull the puck around an object with the toe.
steps: Put a stick or shoe on the floor.
Push the puck toward it, then toe drag it around and past.
Do it to both sides.
why: The move that beats a poke check.

name: Backhand Cradle
summary: Carry and control the puck only on your backhand.
steps: Keep the puck on the backhand side of the blade.
Move it forward, back and side to side without switching to the forehand.
Stay in a skating stance.
why: Strong backhand control makes you unpredictable.

name: Puck Protection Handling
summary: Keep your body between the puck and an imaginary defender.
steps: Wide stance, body turned sideways.
Stickhandle on the far side of your body.
Keep the puck away from where a defender would reach.
why: Winning battles along the boards means hiding the puck.

name: Skate to Stick
summary: Kick the puck from your foot up to your stick.
steps: Pass the puck into your feet.
Kick it from your skate or shoe back up to your blade.
Continue stickhandling.
cues: Angle the foot like a skate blade
why: Saves bad passes and keeps plays alive.

name: Eyes-Closed Stickhandling
summary: Stickhandle in place with your eyes shut.
steps: Start slow with eyes open, then close them.
Stickhandle side to side, feeling the puck.
Open your eyes if you lose it and restart.
why: Builds feel so your eyes can stay on the play.

name: Speed Cone Weave
summary: Weave through cones at max speed with control.
steps: Line up 5 cones a stick-length apart.
Weave through as fast as you can.
Turn and come back on the backhand side.
why: Handling at game speed.

name: One-Hand Figure 8
summary: Figure 8 around two objects with only your top hand.
steps: Two objects a stick-length apart.
Top hand only, stickhandle a figure 8 around them.
Switch to bottom hand only.
why: One-hand control for driving wide and reaching around defenders.

name: Dangle Combo
summary: Chain moves: wide, toe drag, between the legs, finish.
steps: Wide forehand-backhand.
Toe drag back across.
Pull between the legs and recover.
Finish with a quick shot or pass.
why: Building combos makes moves automatic.

name: Easy Jog
summary: Light, relaxed jog.
steps: Jog at a pace you could talk at.
Relax the shoulders and hands.
Keep a quick, light cadence.
why: Recovery and base fitness without stress.

name: 40 m Sprints
summary: All-out 40 m sprints with full recovery.
steps: Start in a staggered stance.
Sprint 40 m at max speed.
Walk back. Full recovery between reps.
why: Pure top speed and acceleration.

name: Flying 20s
summary: Build up for 20 m, then sprint 20 m flat out.
steps: Build speed over 20 m.
Hit max speed through the next 20 m zone.
Walk back and recover.
cues: Tall and relaxed at top speed
why: Trains max velocity, the top gear on a breakaway.

name: Jog-Sprint Intervals
summary: 30 s jog, 15 s sprint, repeat.
steps: Jog easy for 30 seconds.
Sprint hard for 15 seconds.
Repeat for every set (rest is the jog).
why: Mimics the stop-start rhythm of a game.

name: Line Sprints (Suicides)
summary: Sprint to each line and back, getting further each time.
steps: Start at the goal line.
Sprint to the first line and back, then the next, then the next.
Touch every line. Rest between sets.
why: The classic hockey conditioner: acceleration, stops and grit.

name: Stair Runs
summary: Run up stairs or bleachers, walk down.
steps: Run up every step, quick feet.
Walk down carefully to recover.
Switch to every other step for power.
cues: Hold the rail on the way down
why: Leg power and conditioning with less pounding.

name: Backward Run
summary: Run backward with quick steps.
steps: Stay low, chest over toes.
Push back with quick, short steps.
Look over your shoulder now and then.
why: Builds the quads and the backward movement defenders use.

name: Bounding
summary: Exaggerated, springy running strides.
steps: Run with big, powerful strides.
Drive the knee up and push off hard.
Hang in the air on each stride.
why: Stride power that carries over to skating.

name: Walking Knee Drive
summary: Step and drive one knee up hard, rising onto the toes.
steps: Step forward.
Drive the opposite knee up to hip height and rise onto your toes.
Pump the arms like a sprinter.
why: Primes the sprint motion.

name: Crab Walk
summary: Hands and feet, belly up, walk forward and back.
steps: Sit, hands behind you, lift your hips.
Walk forward on hands and feet.
Then go backward.
why: Warms up shoulders and posterior chain.

name: Duck Walk
summary: Walk in a deep squat.
steps: Drop into a deep squat.
Walk forward without standing up.
Keep the chest up.
why: Hip mobility and quad burn in the skating position.

name: Wall Drives
summary: Lean into a wall at 45° and drive one knee up fast.
steps: Hands on a wall, body at about 45°, on the balls of your feet.
Drive one knee up to hip height, toe up.
Punch it back down under your hip. Alternate, or do fast exchanges.
why: Teaches the acceleration body angle and front-side mechanics.

name: Fast Leg Drill
summary: Skip along and cycle one leg through as fast as possible.
steps: Skip lightly forward.
Every third step, cycle one leg through a full fast stride.
Stay tall, alternate legs between sets.
cues: Heel to butt, knee up, step over
why: Builds the quick recovery cycle of top-speed sprinting.

name: Ankling
summary: Small, quick steps rolling over stiff ankles.
steps: Move forward with tiny steps.
Strike the ground under your hips with a stiff ankle.
Keep the knees low and the rhythm fast.
why: Ankle stiffness = less ground contact time = more speed.

name: Block Starts
summary: Explode out of the blocks for 20 m.
steps: Set blocks: front foot about two feet back from the line.
On set, raise hips slightly above shoulders.
Drive out low and push through the full first 10 steps. Walk back.
cues: Low heel recovery out of the blocks
why: The first 10 steps decide short sprints.

name: 3-Point Starts
summary: Accelerate from a three-point stance.
steps: One hand down, opposite leg forward.
Explode forward, staying low.
Rise gradually over 20 m. Walk back.
why: Acceleration practice without blocks.

name: 30 m Accelerations
summary: Build from a standing start to near-max speed in 30 m.
steps: Start from a 2-point stance.
Accelerate hard, rising gradually.
Walk back. Full recovery.
why: Acceleration is trainable, and it's half of every sprint.

name: Flying 30s
summary: 20 m build-up into 30 m at max speed.
steps: Build up over 20 m.
Sprint the next 30 m at true max velocity.
Walk back. 3–5 min rest.
why: Raises your top speed ceiling.

name: 60 m Sprints
summary: Full-effort 60 m.
steps: Start from blocks or a 3-point stance.
Run 60 m all-out.
Full recovery between reps.
why: Race-specific speed for the 60 and 100.

name: 150 m Speed Endurance
summary: Near-max 150s with long rest.
steps: Walk 5–8 minutes between reps.
Stop if times drop off a lot.
why: Teaches you to hold speed at the end of a 200 or 400.

name: Tempo 100s
summary: Smooth 100s at about 70%, walk the curve.
steps: Run the straight at about 70%.
Walk the curve to recover.
Keep every rep the same time.
why: Builds aerobic capacity and recovery without beating up the legs.

name: 300 m Repeats
summary: Hard 300s with full rest. 400 runners' bread and butter.
steps: Run 300 m at 400 m race pace or slightly slower.
Rest 8–10 minutes.
Aim for consistent times.
cues: Drive the arms down the straight
why: Lactate tolerance for the 400.

name: 200 m Repeats
summary: 200s at 85–90% with full recovery.
steps: Run the bend and straight.
Rest 4–6 minutes.
Keep times within a second of each other.
why: Speed endurance for the 200 and 400.

name: Baton Exchanges
summary: Practise relay handoffs at speed.
steps: Outgoing runner marks a check mark and starts on it.
Incoming runner calls 'stick' and passes up or down.
Complete the pass inside the zone at full speed.
why: Relays are won in the exchange zones.

name: Hurdle Walkovers
summary: Step over a row of hurdles with tall posture.
steps: Set 6–8 hurdles at mid height, close together.
Walk over each, lifting the knee high.
Go forward, sideways and backward.
why: Hip mobility that hurdlers (and everyone else) need.

name: Lead Leg Drill
summary: Attack the hurdle with a bent lead knee, then snap it down.
steps: Walk or jog alongside hurdles with the lead leg going over.
Drive the knee up first, then extend the foot.
Snap the leg down quickly after the barrier.
why: A fast lead leg saves time over every hurdle.

name: Trail Leg Drill
summary: Bring the trail leg through flat and fast.
steps: Walk alongside hurdles with the trail leg going over.
Pull the knee through flat, toe turned up and out.
Bring the knee to the front, not the side.
why: A clean trail leg keeps you from clipping hurdles.

name: Hurdle Hops
summary: Two-foot rebound jumps over mini hurdles.
steps: Line up 5–6 low hurdles.
Jump over each with both feet.
Minimal ground contact between jumps.
why: Reactive power and rhythm.

name: 3-Step Rhythm
summary: Run over 3–5 hurdles at reduced spacing, three steps between.
steps: Set hurdles a bit closer than race spacing.
Run over them with three steps between each.
Walk back. Push spacing out as you get faster.
why: Rhythm is everything in the hurdles.

name: Hurdle Mobility Circuit
summary: Over-unders and seated hurdle stretches.
steps: Alternate stepping over one hurdle and ducking under the next.
Finish with seated hurdler stretches.
Do both directions.
why: Keeps the hips open for clean clearance.

name: Approach Runs
summary: Run your full approach without jumping. Hit your marks.
steps: Start on your mark.
Run your full approach at jump speed.
Run through the board. Note where your takeoff foot lands.
why: A consistent approach fixes most fouls and short jumps.

name: Pop-Ups
summary: Short approach, take off, and land on the takeoff leg's opposite.
steps: Use a 4–6 step approach.
Take off and drive the free knee up.
Land in the pit in the 'pop-up' position, no full jump.
why: Grooves the takeoff position.

name: Single-Leg Bounds
summary: Hop for distance on one leg.
steps: Push off one leg.
Cycle the leg through and land on the same leg.
Continue for all reps, then switch.
why: Triple jump power and single-leg elasticity.

name: Standing Triple Jump
summary: Hop, step, jump from a standstill.
steps: Start on one leg.
Hop (same leg), step (other leg), jump (two feet).
Measure and try to beat it.
why: Builds triple-jump rhythm and is a great test.

name: Depth Jumps
summary: Step off a box and rebound up instantly.
steps: Stand on a knee-high box.
Step off, land on both feet.
Jump straight up as fast as possible.
why: Elite reactive power for jumpers and sprinters.

name: High Jump Scissor Drill
summary: Short curved approach, scissor over a low bar.
steps: Run a 3–5 step curve.
Plant the outside foot and drive the inside knee up.
Scissor the legs over a low bar.
cues: Plant and go up, not across
Lean away from the bar on the curve
why: Teaches high jump takeoff without the flop.

name: Box Bounds
summary: Alternate-leg bounds onto low boxes.
steps: Line up 3–4 low boxes.
Bound from the floor to box to floor, alternating legs.
Keep moving forward.
why: Bounding power with height.

name: Overhead Back Toss
summary: Squat with a med ball and throw it backward over your head.
steps: Hold the ball between your legs, quarter squat.
Explode up and throw it back over your head.
Full hip extension, land in a jump.
why: Total-body power. A classic throwers' test.

name: Med Ball Chest Pass
summary: Explosive two-hand pass into a wall.
steps: Stand facing a wall, ball at your chest.
Step and push the ball hard into the wall.
Catch and repeat.
why: Upper-body power for shot put.

name: Rotational Scoop Toss
summary: Load the back hip and sling the ball sideways.
steps: Stand side-on to a wall.
Load the back hip, then rotate hard.
Release at hip height into the wall.
why: Rotational power for discus and hammer.

name: Shot Put Standing Throws
summary: Power-position throws without the glide.
steps: Get into the power position, shot on the neck.
Drive the legs, rotate the hips, then punch the shot.
Finish high, elbow behind the shot.
why: Technique is built from the standing throw out.

name: Discus Turn Drill
summary: Practise the turn without throwing.
steps: Start at the back of the ring.
Pivot on the left foot (right-handed) and sprint across.
Land in the power position.
why: Footwork is where discus distance comes from.

name: Javelin Crossover Steps
summary: Rhythm crossovers with the javelin drawn back.
steps: Withdraw the javelin and run sideways with crossover steps.
Keep the shoulders closed.
Finish with a block step (no throw).
why: Gets your approach rhythm right.

name: Long Run
summary: Your longest run of the week at an easy pace.
steps: Run easy, conversational pace.
Stay steady the whole time.
Fuel and hydrate after.
why: The foundation of distance fitness.

name: 800 m Repeats
summary: Two laps hard, recover, repeat.
steps: Run 800 m at goal mile or 5K pace.
Jog 2–3 minutes.
Keep splits even.
why: VO2 max and pace sense.

name: Mile Repeats
summary: Comfortably hard miles.
steps: Run 1600 m at threshold pace.
Jog 3 minutes.
Repeat.
why: Raises the pace you can hold for a long time.

name: Progression Run
summary: Start easy, finish fast.
steps: Start at an easy pace.
Speed up every 5–10 minutes.
Finish the last few minutes near race pace.
why: Teaches you to close races.

name: Hill Jog Up & Down
summary: Jog up, jog back down, repeat. Endurance on the way up, control on the way down.
steps: Find a hill that takes about 30–60 seconds to jog up.
Up: jog at a steady pace you could keep going at. Short steps, lean from the ankles, swing the arms.
Tap "At the top" when you get there.
Down: jog back with short, quick steps. Stay tall, land softly under your hips and keep it under control. Don't let gravity run you.
Tap "At the bottom". That's one trip.
why: Climbing builds aerobic endurance and leg strength. Coming down teaches your legs to absorb and brake, which protects your knees and helps you stop and change direction.

name: Hill Repeats
summary: Run up strong, jog down under control.
steps: Find a hill that takes 20–40 seconds to run up.
Up: run strong but not all-out. Try to match your first climb time every rep.
Down: jog back down slowly with short steps and recover. Catch yourself, don't fall down the hill.
Start the next climb when your breathing settles.
why: Strength-endurance for the legs and lungs. Watching your climb times shows when you're fading.

name: Hill Sprints
summary: Sprint a short hill, walk down.
steps: Pick a short, moderate hill (about 10–15 seconds of sprinting).
Up: sprint all-out to the top.
Down: walk all the way back. Full recovery keeps every sprint fast.
Stop if your climb time gets much slower than your best.
cues: Full rest on the way down
why: Builds acceleration power with less impact than flat sprints.

name: Long Hill Repeats
summary: A long climb at a hard, steady effort, jog down.
steps: Find a long hill (60–90 seconds up).
Up: run at about 80% effort and hold it the whole way.
Down: jog easy and controlled. Use it to recover and practise braking with short steps.
Try to keep every climb within a few seconds of your first.
why: Raises your aerobic ceiling and lactate tolerance with less pounding than flat intervals.

name: Uphill Power Walk
summary: Walk fast up a steep hill or ramp, easy walk down.
steps: Up: walk as fast as you can without running. Push through the whole foot and squeeze your glutes.
Down: walk down slowly and in control, knees soft.
Repeat for the number of trips.
why: Low-impact endurance that builds glutes and calves. Good on recovery days.

name: Backward Hill Walk
summary: Walk backwards up the hill, walk down normally.
steps: Face down the hill.
Up: walk backwards, landing on the balls of your feet, knees bent, chest up.
Down: turn around and walk down normally.
why: Strengthens the quads and knees with very little joint stress.

name: Hill Bounds
summary: Springy bounds up a gentle slope, walk down.
steps: Use a gentle hill.
Up: push off one leg and drive the other knee up and forward, landing on the opposite foot. Keep bounding to the top.
Down: walk back and rest fully.
why: Builds single-leg power and stride length. The slope makes landings softer.

name: Uphill Lateral Shuffle
summary: Shuffle sideways up the hill, walk down.
steps: Stand sideways to the hill in an athletic stance.
Up: shuffle without crossing your feet.
Down: walk back and face the other way next time.
why: Trains the lateral push used in skating strides and defensive slides.

name: Wrist Circles
summary: Loose circles with both wrists, both directions.
steps: Make loose fists with your arms out in front.
Circle both wrists slowly for 15 seconds.
Reverse the direction for 15 seconds.
why: Gets blood into the wrists before shooting or stickhandling.

name: Dumbbell Wrist Rotations
summary: Hold one end of a dumbbell and turn your palm up, then down.
steps: Sit with your forearm on your thigh and your hand past the knee.
Hold a light dumbbell by one end, like a hammer, pointing up.
Slowly turn your palm all the way down, then all the way up. That's one rep.
why: Turning the wrist over (pronation and supination) is the motion behind roll-overs on a wrist shot and saucer passes.

name: Stick Wrist Rotations
summary: Hold a stick in one hand and rotate it side to side.
steps: Hold your stick straight up with one hand, a hand-width up from the bottom.
Elbow bent at 90 degrees, tucked at your side.
Slowly tip the stick to one side, then the other, turning only your wrist and forearm.
cues: Choke up to make it easier
why: The stick is a long lever, so even small wrist turns build a lot of rotational strength.

name: Stick Levers
summary: Hold the end of the stick and tip the blade up and down.
steps: Stand with your arm at your side holding the top of the stick, blade in front.
Lift the blade up by bending only your wrist.
Lower slowly. Then turn around so the blade is behind you and repeat.
why: Trains the thumb-side and pinky-side wrist muscles that hold the blade steady when you take a hit or shoot.

name: Towel Wring
summary: Twist a towel hard one way, then the other.
steps: Hold a rolled towel in both hands, arms in front.
Wring it as hard as you can, like squeezing out water.
Hold for a second, then twist the other way. Each direction is one rep.
why: Rotation and grip together, with no equipment. Good for hotel rooms.

name: Band Finger Extensions
summary: Spread your fingers against a small band or rubber band.
steps: Loop a light band or rubber band around your fingers and thumb.
Spread your fingers open as wide as you can.
Close slowly.
why: Balances all the gripping. Helps keep wrists and elbows healthy.

name: Wrist Flexor & Extensor Stretch
summary: Pull your fingers back, then your hand down, arm straight.
steps: Arm straight out, palm up. Use your other hand to gently pull your fingers back. Hold 10 seconds.
Flip your palm down and pull the back of your hand toward you. Hold 10 seconds.
Switch arms.
why: Loosens the forearms after shooting, stickhandling or grip work.

name: C-Skips
summary: Skip and swing the knee up and out in a C shape.
steps: Skip forward like an A-skip.
Lift the knee up in front, then open it out to the side and bring the foot back down, so the knee draws a C.
Alternate legs. Go both forward (knee opens out) and backward (knee comes across).
cues: Open the hip, not the back
why: Opens the hips through the hurdle trail-leg motion and warms up the groin. Good before hurdles, sprints or skating.
